stories.headline: PT holds 8th National Congress, approves moderated 2026 manifesto focused on Lula reelection
stories.summary: The Workers' Party convened its three-day national congress in Brasília (April 24-26), approving a manifesto entitled 'Construindo o Futuro' that centers on Lula's reelection, makes rhetorical overtures to centrist parties, and quietly dropped references to the Banco Master scandal and overt financial system reform demands at the Planalto's request. Lula, recovering from medical procedures, participated only via pre-recorded video, while VP Alckmin pledged loyalty and ex-Finance Minister Haddad attacked Flávio Bolsonaro as 'Bolsonarinho.' Party president Edinho Silva called for humility toward evangelicals and app workers, and a Maduro-support banner at the venue triggered opposition criticism.

stories.headline: Lula undergoes skin cancer removal and wrist procedure, discharged same day
stories.summary: President Lula entered Hospital Sírio-Libanês in São Paulo on April 24 for two procedures: removal of a basal cell carcinoma (a common, non-metastatic skin cancer) from his scalp and a cortisone injection in his right thumb for tendinitis. His doctor Roberto Kalil said the procedures were simple, the president was in good humor, and there would be no impact on his schedule. Lula was discharged the same day and returned to Brasília by April 26.

stories.headline: Multiple polls show Flávio Bolsonaro leading or tied with Lula in key states ahead of 2026 election
stories.summary: A series of polls released this week (Paraná Pesquisas, Vox Brasil, Datafolha, Genial/Quaest) showed Flávio Bolsonaro leading or in a technical tie with President Lula in São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, with Lula polling weaker among northeastern voters than in 2022. Analysts note the race is fluid with the election in October, and the government is hoping new popular measures (such as the 6x1 schedule reform and 'blusinha tax' review) will improve Lula's standing.

stories.headline: Brazil-US diplomatic crisis over Ramagem arrest escalates to agent expulsions, then de-escalates
stories.summary: A diplomatic crisis stemming from the arrest of ex-ABIN chief Alexandre Ramagem (convicted by the STF in the coup-plot case) in Florida deepened this week: the US expelled PF delegate Marcelo Ivo who assisted in the arrest, Brazil's Itamaraty immediately applied reciprocity by stripping credentials from US immigration agent Michael Myers, and Lula publicly endorsed the measure. By April 24, Myers had left Brazil. Lula also said he hoped the US would return to dialogue to 'normalize bilateral relations,' while analysts noted the episode exposed ongoing Bolsonaro-aligned influence within the Trump administration.

stories.headline: Bolsonaro awaits STF authorization for shoulder surgery while STM weighs potential loss of military rank
stories.summary: Former president Jair Bolsonaro, under house arrest since March, sought court approval to leave confinement for surgery on a torn rotator cuff; the Solicitor General (PGR) endorsed the request and it awaits STF Justice Alexandre de Moraes' decision. Separately, the Superior Military Tribunal (STM) authorized collection of military service documents to evaluate whether Bolsonaro should lose his captain's reserve rank following his STF conviction in the coup-plot case. Justice Cármen Lúcia also rejected a habeas corpus petition aimed at modifying his house arrest conditions.

stories.headline: Right-wing fracture widens as Nikolas Ferreira clashes with Bolsonaro family, Flávio calls for unity
stories.summary: A public feud escalated this week between deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) and the Bolsonaro family: Nikolas called Jair Renan a 'blind mole,' drawing responses from Carlos Bolsonaro who accused him of being an 'opportunist,' while Flávio Bolsonaro published an appeal for unity among the right. Michelle Bolsonaro's promotion of a Bolsonaro rival in Santa Catarina and Flávio's own acknowledgment that 'support cannot be imposed' added to the picture of internal PL tensions ahead of the 2026 presidential race.

stories.headline: STF becomes central 2026 campaign target as Zema escalates satirical attacks and court divides on response
stories.summary: Pre-candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) published a new installment of his AI-and-puppet video series satirizing STF ministers Gilmar Mendes and Alexandre de Moraes as 'untouchables,' defying Gilmar's request to be included in the fake-news inquiry. STF ministers are internally divided between those who favor a firm institutional response and those who believe engaging amplifies the attacks. The PT also announced it would propose a judicial ethics code for the STF in its government program, signaling a cross-spectrum political alignment against the court ahead of October.

stories.headline: Senate CCJ to hold confirmation hearing for Lula's STF nominee Jorge Messias on April 29
stories.summary: The Senate's Constitution and Justice Committee is scheduled to hear Jorge Messias, Brazil's current Solicitor General and Lula's nominee to the STF, on April 29 — more than five months after his nomination. Messias has been lobbying senators for votes and is expected to be confirmed, with the Lula government's liaison minister Zé Guimarães saying negotiations are on track for approval.
